title: Range masks: picking and the unbound stage
objective: Make luminance and colour range masks usable as created: an unbound mask reads its input at the position a first Basic adjustment would take, creating a range mask selects it, shows Tint and arms a Lightroom-style eyedropper in Mask mode, and each click or drag on the photograph is one pick command with one history entry, reachable from the API.
context_summary: The owner reported on 2026-10-16 that colour and luminance range masks did not seem to work. The core and the CPU reference are correct; the desktop flow hides them: creation is behind the off-by-default experiment masks.range-selections, a new range component is not selected, an unbound mask's overlay, thumbnail, Pick and colour-held brush are refused until an adjustment is bound (refusal only in the event log), Tint is never turned on for a typed creation, the overlay hides while the selection's own controls are dragged, and Pick leaves Mask mode. The owner decided on 2026-10-16: creation stays behind the flag, off by default; Lightroom-style picking (colour click replaces, Shift+click adds up to five, drag samples an area; luminance click sets a band around the tone, drag sets the band to the area's span; Escape, Enter or Done ends picking; band slider, fields, swatches and Refine remain); and this reverses P17's refusal of an unbound mask. Derivation constants, the colour-stage input site, the canvas details and the panel wording are delegated choices recorded in docs/design/range-masks.md; the board is docs/design/develop-workspace/range-masks.png. The selection equations of the range study stay frozen. No external input blocks delivery: the range fixture and generated JPEGs suffice; M4 GPU device evidence, corpus qualification and measurement come last with no dependency back into delivery. Re-review each task against current main before starting, as the roadmap's ready-to-implement section says, and use its minimum model.

tasks.description: Replace input_layer_index with an input site that answers unbound masks, and thread its explicit mode through every reader.
extra_context: Add input_site(registry, recipe, mask) -> Result<InputSite { index, mode }, Error> beside the current input_layer_index in crates/luxforge-core/src/mask/commands/plan.rs and remove input_layer_index. A bound mask: the first bound layer in evaluation order, mode from render::MaskInputMode::for_layer. An unbound mask: the minimum of ModuleRegistry::insertion_index_for_target(layers, effect, Some(mask), masks) over registered maskable effects of EffectStage::Color, mode ColourRun passed explicitly (for_layer at a not-yet-inserted index answers for whichever layer sits there). With no colour-stage maskable effect, the earliest maskable effect of any stage with its stage's mode; with none maskable, a refusal by name from a new mask::rules function.

The colour-stage restriction is deliberate: Detail is maskable at EffectStage::Restoration, so the earliest maskable position of any stage would be Detail's, and binding a first Basic adjustment would then move the site past the global Basic layer. With the colour-stage rule, binding a first Basic adjustment leaves coverage identical.
Remove rules::bound_layer and rules::limit_on_new_mask; a colour-held stroke on a new mask seeds from the input site. Keep P16's refusal of a first bound layer behind a later spatial layer.

Every reader takes the site and its explicit mode instead of calling for_layer on the index: preview/coverage.rs (overlay and the thumbnail key), render/entry.rs layer_input, render/input_grid.rs GridRequest, tiles/region.rs RegionRequest and read, editor/pixels.rs (PixelReadKey, the mask.sample-input path and TileStage::read), editor/masks.rs (the seed and mask_input_sample) and editor/plan.rs HostStage reads through StageQuestions. The GPU path needs no change: ReadStage::Before already carries the mode.

Render and export are unaffected: a mask with no bound layer modulates nothing. Update the mask.sample-input and constrained-brush notes in the host descriptor so their schema text states the input-site rule. Update docs/design/masking.md's rule text and docs/design/range-masks.md's status for this part; leave the shared docs to the integrator.
Implementer chooses the struct and helper names and where the per-reader mode is carried, within this contract.

acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover each branch of input_site: bound (first bound layer and its mode), unbound with Basic registered (Basic's masked position after the global Basic layer and earlier masks' Basic layers, ColourRun), no colour-stage maskable effect, and none maskable (the named refusal).

An exact-buffer reference test shows an unbound range mask's coverage grid and thumbnail grid are byte-identical before and after a first masked Basic adjustment is bound; a first masked Tone curve binding moves the site to that layer.
A Detail-led stack's unbound site reads through the bounded input grid; P16's spatial-prefix refusal still holds for a bound mask behind Presence.
mask.sample-input and a colour-held stroke on a new or unbound mask answer from the input site instead of being refused; the constrained-brush seed of a bound mask is unchanged.
Rendered and exported bytes of a recipe are unchanged by creating an unbound range mask on it.
No reader calls MaskInputMode::for_layer for a mask's input outside input_site; existing mask, overlay, input-grid and region tests pass.

tasks.description: Add the read-only mask.sample-input-area query, the generated mask.pick-<kind> commands with their pure derivations, and the AreaPick canvas declaration.
extra_context: Consumes TASK-001's input site: both commands read at it, so they work on unbound masks.

mask.sample-input-area {asset_id, mask, x, y, width, height}: normalized content coordinates; answers linear r, g, b per point in reading order, the power-of-two reduction (the smallest leaving at most 4,096 points), the reduced size and the renderer record. Answered by the tile service on the desktop (GPU as renderer of record) and the reference elsewhere, through tiles::region with the site's explicit mode. Clip to the stage; refuse a rectangle wholly outside it. Read-only: no history, no event.

mask.pick-<kind> {asset_id, mask, component, x, y, width?, height?, add?, mutation} is generated from a new pick entry in the host kind table (crates/luxforge-core/src/mask/mod.rs COMPONENT_KINDS) for luminance-range and colour-range. Absent width/height is a click at the content pixel holding (x, y). add is declared only by kinds that hold samples. It reads through the existing deferred pixel-read path (owner bookkeeping, replay with entry/revision/draft/source checks), commits one history entry labelled 'Pick <Component name>' with the mask prefix rule other mask.* labels follow, and is never gated by masks.range-selections.

Derivations are pure functions in crates/luxforge-core/src/mask/range.rs over the band's 0..100 tone axis and the Oklab (a, b) metric. Luminance click: low = e - 10, high = e + 10 clamped to 0..100, both shoulders 10. Luminance drag: low/high the 5th/95th percentile tones, shoulders kept but raised to 2 where narrower. Colour click: samples = [pixel] or appended with add; a held colour changes nothing; a sixth is refused by rules::room_for_sample; Refine unchanged. Colour drag: the medoid (the reduced point nearest the area's mean (a, b)) as the sample, replace or add; Refine := min(Refine, refine_for(d90 / PLATEAU)) with refine_for(r) = 100 * ln(r / RADIUS_MAX) / ln(RADIUS_MIN / RADIUS_MAX) clamped to 0..100 and r = 0 giving 100. The frozen selection equations do not change.

Add CanvasInteraction::AreaPick {action, title}; the host declares one per kind with a pick entry in place of its SampleApply declarations (mask/commands/declare.rs canvas and canvas_pick). Modules keep SampleApply. mask.add-<kind>-sample, mask.delete-<kind>-sample and mask.sample-input stay. Validation, schema.list and module.list publish the new query, commands and interaction.

Removing the host SampleApply declarations leaves the desktop's host sample pick (PickTarget::HostSample, CanvasPick::HostSample) unreachable; make only the changes needed for the workspace to build and its tests to pass. The desktop has no range pick between this task and TASK-004, which builds the picker on the same branch before the feature is integrated.
Implementer chooses the answer's field names, percentile convention and tie-breaks within this contract, and records them in the design.

acceptance_criteria: Derivation unit tests match hand-computed values: band clamping at 0 and 100, percentiles on a known tone set, the shoulder floor, medoid selection on a two-coloured set, d90, refine_for at r = 0, at RADIUS_MAX and beyond, and Refine never raised.

mask.sample-input-area answers at most 4,096 points with the reduction stated, clips to the stage, refuses a rectangle outside it, writes no history and reports its renderer; reference answers are exact against an independent prefix render.

Each mask.pick-<kind> commits exactly one entry with its label on both bound and unbound masks; a duplicate colour changes nothing; a sixth sample is refused with the room_for_sample sentence; picks succeed with masks.range-selections off.
The host descriptor validates; schema.list and module.list list the query, both pick commands and one AreaPick per range kind; no host SampleApply remains; Basic's neutral picker is unchanged.
A JSON request from an independent client and the same pick through the command service produce the same stack, history and pixels.

expected_results: Query, pick and derivation tests pass; the descriptor validates and the workspace builds with host SampleApply removed.

tasks.description: Select created and added range components, keep the overlay while the mask's own controls are dragged, and show coverage refusals on the mask row and status bar.
extra_context: Independent of the core tasks; it changes desktop view state only.

Creating a typed kind selects its new component: open_created_mask (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/masks.rs) sets selected_component to the created mask's first component instead of None. Adding a component to the open mask selects the added component through the same post-commit path in crates/luxforge-app/src/app/sync.rs that detects a created mask.

mask_adjustment_held (app/masks.rs) returns true only for module-section sliders; mask-family controls (band grips and range fields, the selection's number fields, Refine and the whole-mask Amount) keep the overlay. Update docs/design/masking-interactions.md's suppression sentence to say which controls suppress.

When coverage is unavailable for the open mask, show the host's refusal as a muted note on the open mask's row and in the status bar, not only in the event log. Today the main cases are an unbound value-based mask and a first bound layer behind a spatial layer; after TASK-001 the unbound case disappears and the others remain, so the note takes whatever reason the coverage worker reports.

tasks.description: Build the range picker as a Mask-mode sub-state with its canvas widget, pick bar and Pick buttons, and remove the host sample pick mode.
extra_context: Consumes TASK-002's mask.pick-<kind> commands and AreaPick declarations, and TASK-003's component selection and overlay rule.

Add MaskPanel.picker: Option<RangePicker { mask, component, kind, map, entry }>: a sub-state of Mask mode. The workspace mode, the adjustment sections' target and the coverage target stay unchanged while it is armed. Arm it after a typed create or add of a kind with an AreaPick and from the row's Pick button. End it on Escape, Enter or Done, on leaving Mask mode, on selecting another mask or component, when the component is deleted or undone away, on another mask gesture and on a photograph change.
effective_overlay shows Tint while the picker is armed unless the person explicitly chose Off (overlay_manual).

New canvas widget crates/luxforge-app/src/view/range_pick_canvas.rs: crosshair cursor, a dashed accent rectangle while dragging, a press moved less than 3 pt is a click, Shift read from the modifiers at release, the drag's corners mapped through the held geometry map and sent as their content-space bounding box. Escape during a drag cancels it and sends nothing, keeping the picker armed. One pick in flight; a pick made meanwhile waits, the newest replacing an older waiting one. Resting handles are not hit targets while picking.

Panel per the board (docs/design/develop-workspace/range-masks.png): a one-line pick bar under the selected row with the accent eyedropper glyph, the kind's hint ('Click a tone · drag over an area' or 'Click a colour · Shift-click to add · drag over an area' with the 'N of 5' count) and Done; a Pick button on luminance and colour rows; the colour row note 'Pick a colour to select' with no samples.

Remove PickTarget::HostSample (app/pointer.rs) and CanvasPick::HostSample (state/tools.rs) with whatever TASK-002 left of them; module picks, including a module pick entered with a mask open (pick_on_mask), are unchanged. Captured frames report the picker state and the drag rectangle. Update docs/design/masking-workspace.md's component-row and range-widget text to delivered behaviour.
Widgets stay plain data in luxforge-ui where shared; the editor decides what a press means. Routine layout and naming are delegated.
